explainer.heading: The story in brief
explainer.body: Sue and Johnsy, two young artists, share a small third-floor flat in a charming old house. One November Johnsy falls seriously ill with pneumonia and loses the will to live. She counts the leaves falling from an old ivy creeper and believes she will die when the last one falls. An old painter, Behrman, secretly paints a leaf on the wall during a stormy night. The leaf never falls, Johnsy recovers — but Behrman dies of pneumonia.
explainer.example: Theme: hope, friendship and sacrifice; art that saves a life.

explainer.heading: Johnsy’s illness
explainer.body: The doctor tells Sue that Johnsy has stubbornly decided she will not get well; without the will to live, no medicine can help. Sue tries to cheer her, then paints in her room, whistling. Johnsy counts backwards — twelve, eleven… five — as leaves fall from the ivy on the brick wall opposite.
explainer.example: “When the last leaf falls, I will die.”

explainer.heading: Behrman
explainer.body: Behrman is a sixty-year-old painter on the ground floor whose lifelong dream of painting a masterpiece was never fulfilled. Sue tells him about Johnsy; he is aghast: “How can she be so foolish?” That night there is a storm.

explainer.heading: The leaf that would not fall
explainer.body: Next morning one green, healthy-looking leaf is still on the creeper, even after another fiercer storm. Johnsy realises she has been wrong — “it is a sin to want to die” — eats soup and wants to look presentable. The doctor says she will recover, but Behrman has pneumonia too.

explainer.heading: The surprise ending
explainer.body: Behrman dies two days later. He was found with wet clothes and shoes, shivering; a ladder, brushes and green and yellow paint lay nearby. Sue explains: the leaf never flutters in the wind because Behrman painted it the night the last real leaf fell — his masterpiece.
explainer.example: O. Henry is famous for surprise (twist) endings.

explainer.heading: Vocabulary & grammar
explainer.body: Collocations: pursue a career, lose hope, make an effort, take care of. Prepositional phrases: in spite of, on purpose, at risk, in need of. Antonyms: hopeful–hopeless, recover–worsen. Grammar — past perfect continuous: had been + verb-ing, for an action that continued up to a point in the past.
explainer.example: Johnsy had been lying in bed for days when Sue called Behrman.
explainer.hook: had been + -ing = long action before another past action.

explainer.heading: Writing & author
explainer.body: An informal email: To / Subject / greeting (Hi…), friendly opening, paragraphs with news, closing line, sign-off (Love / Take care). O. Henry (William Sydney Porter) was an American short-story writer of the early 20th century. Works: Cabbages and Kings, The Four Million, The Trimmed Lamp, “The Gift of the Magi”.

questions.q: What do the falling leaves symbolise for Johnsy?
questions.model: For Johnsy the falling leaves stand for her own life slipping away; she believes that when the last leaf falls, she too will die. They symbolise her hopelessness.
points: When the last falls she will die → hopelessness

questions.q: How did Sue try to change Johnsy’s pessimistic attitude?
questions.model: Sue talked to her cheerfully, brought her soup, told her the doctor was confident, painted in her room while whistling a cheerful tune, and asked her not to look out of the window.
points: Brought soup / painted & whistled / asked her not to look out

questions.q: How did Behrman save Johnsy’s life? Why is the leaf called his masterpiece?
questions.model: Sue told Behrman that Johnsy believed she would die when the last leaf fell. On the stormy night when the last real leaf fell, Behrman climbed a ladder in the rain and painted a green leaf on the wall. Johnsy saw that the “leaf” survived two storms and realised she had been wrong to want to die; she regained hope and recovered. Behrman caught pneumonia and died. It is his masterpiece because he had always dreamt of painting one, and this painting was so real it saved a life — at the cost of his own.
points: Learned of Johnsy’s belief from Sue
Painted the leaf on the wall in the stormy night
Leaf gave Johnsy hope → recovery; Behrman died of pneumonia
Masterpiece: lifelong dream; so real it saved a life (sacrifice)
